data.best_text: June to August for the fjord and the islands, February to March for skiing at Holmenkollen.
data.day_budget_note: Per person per day excluding flights: a share of a mid-range double room, food, local transport and one sight. A rough estimate.

stay.label: Weekend
stay.text: The Opera House, MUNCH and Vigeland Park.

stay.label: Long weekend
stay.text: Time for island hopping in the fjord and Holmenkollen.

stay.label: Five days
stay.text: Add the Bygdøy museums and a day in Nordmarka.

areas.name: Sentrum
areas.text: Close to Oslo S and the airport train, walking distance to the Opera House.

areas.name: Grünerløkka
areas.text: Cafés, bars and second-hand shops. Tram into the centre.

areas.name: Frogner and Majorstuen
areas.text: Quiet and close to Vigeland Park. More expensive.

areas.name: Around Brugata and lower Grønland
areas.text: Rowdier in the evenings. Good for cheap food, worse to stay in.

transport.text: 19 minutes to Oslo S, departing every ten minutes for most of the day.
About 23 minutes to Oslo S and usually costs roughly half as much as Flytoget.

events.name: Holmenkollen Ski Festival
events.text: World Cup in cross-country, ski jumping and Nordic combined.

events.name: Holmenkollstafetten
events.text: A big relay race through the city. Streets along the course are closed.

events.name: National Day, 17 May
events.text: The children's parade passes the palace and the whole city is out. Much is closed.

seasons.name: Ski season
seasons.text: Cross-country tracks in Nordmarka and slopes at Holmenkollen.

seasons.name: Swimming and boats to the islands

month_notes: Cold and snowy. The ski tracks in Nordmarka are open.
The best month for skiing. Cold but lighter.
The snow melts. Grey before things turn green.
Green and bright. National Day is celebrated on 17 May.
Bright evenings. The boats run to the islands in the fjord.
Warmest. Swimming in the fjord, but many Oslo residents are away.
Autumn colours in the forest and fewer tourists.
Dark and wet before the snow arrives.

prices.summary: Eating out is expensive, and alcohol is the most expensive of all.
tips: A double room costs around 210 dollars per night on average according to Kayak. The source gives no breakdown by hotel class.

NO-fakta-inresa.title: Passport or national ID card
NO-fakta-inresa.summary: Bring a passport or national ID card. A driving licence does not normally count as a travel document.
NO-fakta-inresa.body: A national ID card is valid for travel within the EU and Schengen, which also includes Iceland and Norway. Within the Nordics a Swedish driving licence can be enough in some cases, but a passport or national ID card is recommended.

NO-fakta-mobil.title: Use data and call as at home
NO-fakta-mobil.summary: The same price as in Sweden for calls, texts and data.
NO-fakta-mobil.body: Roam-like-at-home also applies in the EEA countries Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. Check whether your plan has a cap on data abroad.

NO-fakta-betala.title: Currency: Norwegian krone (NOK)
NO-fakta-betala.summary: The country uses the Norwegian krone (NOK).

NO-fakta-alkohol-18.title: Beer and wine from age 18
NO-fakta-alkohol-18.summary: Age 18 for drinks below 22 per cent.
NO-fakta-alkohol-18.body: The age limit is 18 for beer, wine and cider. Everything above 4.7 per cent is sold only at Vinmonopolet.

NO-fakta-alkohol-20.title: Spirits from age 20
NO-fakta-alkohol-20.summary: Age 20 for drinks of 22 per cent or more.
NO-fakta-alkohol-20.body: The limit applies to both purchase and serving. Buying for minors is prohibited.

NO-oslo-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Gardermoen to Oslo S in 19 minutes
NO-oslo-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: Flytoget takes 19 minutes. Ordinary regional trains take a few minutes longer and are cheaper.
NO-oslo-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: Flytoget runs every ten minutes. Vy's regional trains take about 23 minutes and usually cost roughly half. The Oslo Pass is valid on Vy trains but not on Flytoget.

NO-fakta-varldsarv.title: Among the first in the world
NO-fakta-varldsarv.summary: Urnes Stave Church and Bryggen became World Heritage Sites as early as 1979.
NO-fakta-varldsarv.body: They were inscribed as numbers 58 and 59 on the World Heritage List. Norway has eight World Heritage Sites.

NO-oslo-fakta-bygdoybaten.title: The Bygdøy boat needs its own ticket
NO-oslo-fakta-bygdoybaten.summary: Boat B9 to Bygdøy is not included in Ruter's tickets.
NO-oslo-fakta-bygdoybaten.body: The island boats B1 and B2 run on an ordinary Ruter ticket, but B9 to Bygdøy does not. With the Oslo Pass, B9 is free.

NO-bryggen.name: Bryggen in Bergen
NO-bryggen.summary: The wooden quarter from the Hanseatic era, a World Heritage Site since 1979.
NO-bryggen.body: One of northern Europe's oldest trading ports with well-preserved wooden buildings.

NO-vestnorsk-fjordlandskap.name: Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord
NO-vestnorsk-fjordlandskap.summary: Norway's only natural heritage site on the list, since 2005.
NO-vestnorsk-fjordlandskap.body: Two areas that together are called the West Norwegian Fjords.

NO-urnes-stavkyrka.name: Urnes Stave Church
NO-urnes-stavkyrka.summary: A World Heritage Site since 1979, in Luster by the Sognefjord.
NO-urnes-stavkyrka.body: The church is open to visitors.

NO-roros.name: Røros Mining Town
NO-roros.summary: A mining town from the 17th century, a World Heritage Site since 1980.
NO-roros.body: The site was extended in 2010 with the landscape around the town, the Circumference.

NO-alta.name: The rock carvings in Alta
NO-alta.body: Rock art far north in Finnmark.

NO-vegaoyan.name: Vegaøyan
NO-vegaoyan.summary: Norway's first cultural landscape on the list, 2004.
NO-vegaoyan.body: An archipelago where eider down has been gathered for generations, work mainly carried out by women.

NO-rjukan-notodden.name: Rjukan–Notodden
NO-rjukan-notodden.summary: Industrial heritage, a World Heritage Site since 2015.
NO-rjukan-notodden.body: Norway's most recent World Heritage Site.

NO-oslo-vigelandsparken.name: Vigeland Park
NO-oslo-vigelandsparken.summary: More than 200 sculptures by Gustav Vigeland. Free and open around the clock.
NO-oslo-vigelandsparken.body: This is where Sinnataggen and the Monolith stand. The park is in Frogner Park and is one of Norway's most visited sights.

NO-oslo-oyhopping.name: Island hopping in the Oslofjord
NO-oslo-oyhopping.summary: The boats to the islands run on an ordinary Ruter ticket.
NO-oslo-oyhopping.body: Line B1 runs all year to Hovedøya and Gressholmen among others. Buy a ticket beforehand, there are no machines on the islands, and do not miss the last boat back.

NO-oslo-operahuset.name: The Opera House
NO-oslo-operahuset.summary: Walk up onto the roof. It is free and built for it.
NO-oslo-operahuset.body: The building opened in 2008 in Bjørvika, and the roof rises out of the fjord like an iceberg. A five-minute walk from Oslo S.

NO-oslo-munch.name: MUNCH
NO-oslo-munch.summary: The Scream and the rest of Munch's art on 13 floors. Book a time slot in advance.
NO-oslo-munch.body: The museum admits visitors in time slots and cannot guarantee entry without a pre-booked ticket. Free admission under 18. With the Oslo Pass you collect a ticket on site and may have to wait 15–30 minutes.

NO-oslo-holmenkollen.name: Holmenkollen
NO-oslo-holmenkollen.summary: A ski museum and a view from the top of the ski jump.
NO-oslo-holmenkollen.body: Take metro line 1 to Holmenkollen and walk about 10 minutes steeply uphill. The museum shows Norway's oldest ski, over 5,000 years old, and the lift goes up the jump tower.

NO-oslo-akershus.name: Akershus Fortress
NO-oslo-akershus.summary: A medieval castle in the middle of the city. The grounds are free.
NO-oslo-akershus.body: Construction began in 1299 under Håkon V. Museums and events inside the grounds have their own tickets.

mat-brunost.name: Brunost
mat-brunost.hint: A brown, sweet cheese that is sliced thin.

bakverk-skillingsbolle.name: Skillingsbolle
bakverk-skillingsbolle.hint: A large cinnamon bun from Bergen.

mat-norsk-vaffel.name: Norwegian waffle
mat-norsk-vaffel.hint: Soft and heart-shaped, ideally with brunost.

naturfenomen-fjord.name: Fjord
naturfenomen-fjord.hint: A narrow inlet of the sea with steep mountainsides.

sevardhet-stavkyrka.name: Stave church
sevardhet-stavkyrka.hint: A medieval wooden church with a tiered roof.

NO-oslo-ide-helg.title: Oslo over the weekend
NO-oslo-ide-helg.body: Take the regional train from Gardermoen instead of Flytoget and spend the money on food.

NO-ide-fjordresa.title: The fjords from Bergen
NO-ide-fjordresa.body: Start at Bryggen and continue towards the Nærøyfjord.

NO-oslo-ide-vigeland.title: Sculpture walk in Vigeland Park
NO-oslo-ide-vigeland.body: Find Sinnataggen and walk all the way up to the Monolith.

NO-oslo-ide-oyhopping.title: Swimming and a picnic on Hovedøya
NO-oslo-ide-oyhopping.body: Take the boat from Aker Brygge with an ordinary ticket. Best in summer, when the boats run late.

NO-oslo-ide-bjorvika.title: Bjørvika: the opera roof and MUNCH
NO-oslo-ide-bjorvika.body: Go up onto the opera roof first and then take the pre-booked museum visit next door.

NO-oslo-ide-holmenkollen.title: The metro up to Holmenkollen
NO-oslo-ide-holmenkollen.body: Ride line 1 up through the forest, see the museum and the view from the jump tower.

NO-oslo-ide-akershus.title: Evening walk at Akershus
NO-oslo-ide-akershus.body: Walk around the fortress grounds and look out over the fjord.

NO-present-brunost.name: Brunost
NO-present-brunost.body: A sweet, brown whey cheese that is sliced thin.

NO-present-ull.name: Knitted wool
NO-present-ull.body: Mittens or socks in a Norwegian pattern take up the least space.

NO-present-mugg.name: Enamel mug with a mountain motif
